title: fix(ext-proc): select standalone cache-salt forwarding by tokenizer backend
body:
## Problem

Standalone EPP resolves an effective `cache_namespace` from the request body and headers, then uses it for KV-aware selection.

Today, its `PickResult` unconditionally uses the native-vLLM forwarding policy. That causes ext-proc to inject vLLM's top-level `cache_salt` extension (`dynamo-cache-salt:<namespace>`) even when standalone EPP uses the SGLang tokenizer/renderer.

SGLang does not currently have a compatible cache-salt request and KV-event contract. Forwarding the vLLM extension to it is therefore incorrect.

## Desired behavior

Derive cache-salt forwarding from the standalone tokenizer/renderer protocol:

- `VllmRender` -> `CacheSaltForwarding::NativeVllm`
  - Inject the resolved, Dynamo-prefixed top-level `cache_salt` for raw vLLM.
- `SglangRenderer` -> `CacheSaltForwarding::NativeSglang`
  - Keep the resolved namespace for Dynamo selection only.
  - Do not inject or overwrite `cache_salt` in the forwarded request body.
- Dynamo runtime continues using `CacheSaltForwarding::Preserve`; downstream workers resolve and tag the original cache-salt inputs.

This relies on the standalone configuration invariant that the tokenizer/renderer protocol matches the registered worker backend.

## Scope

This does not add end-to-end cache-salt isolation for raw SGLang. It prevents EPP from sending vLLM's extension to SGLang while preserving correct namespace-aware selection. SGLang cache-salt forwarding and matching KV-event representation should be investigated separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add `CacheSaltForwarding::NativeSglang`.
- Select the forwarding policy from `RendererProtocol` when constructing standalone `EppRouter`.
- `inject_body_extensions` receives a cache salt only for `NativeVllm`.
- Add focused coverage for the renderer-protocol-to-forwarding-policy mapping.

title: bug(request-trace): tool-event tasks can be skipped during runtime handoff
body:
External contributor ayaangazali has an open implementation in ai-dynamo/dynamo#13445, checked September 18, 2026. The September 8 revision makes initialization fail when the previously observed task owner has cancelled and adds a deterministic regression. It deliberately chooses failure instead of automatic re-arming.

Review ownership reassigned to Ishan Dhanani on September 18, 2026, at Matej’s request. Ishan is an agents, observability, and runtime codeowner and has contributed extensively to the affected request-trace implementation.

The remaining work is review of that lifecycle contract and the existing contribution. This is separate from the sink-worker restart defect in ai-dynamo/dynamo#13372, now delivered through PR ai-dynamo/dynamo#14642. The original report follows.

## Description

The request-trace tool-event relay and ingest tasks can both be skipped when a replacement distributed runtime starts while the preceding runtime is still completing cancellation.

Each task uses a process-global `AtomicBool` as its startup guard. The guard is set before task creation and cleared inside the old task only after that task observes runtime cancellation and reaches its final cleanup statement. During the interval between cancellation and cleanup, a replacement call sees the guard as `true`, logs that the task is already started, and returns `Ok(())`. Once the old task resumes, it clears the guard and exits; the replacement runtime has already returned from initialization and does not retry.

The two guards can race independently:

* [`REQUEST_TRACE_TOOL_EVENT_INGEST_STARTED`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/a5228ae9f6354f91ff792fd0d3636264b27a14d4/lib/llm/src/request_trace/agent_context.rs#L186-L187>) remains set until the old ingest loop exits and reaches its final store at [lines 427–458](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/a5228ae9f6354f91ff792fd0d3636264b27a14d4/lib/llm/src/request_trace/agent_context.rs#L427-L458>).
* [`TOOL_EVENT_RELAY_STARTED`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/a5228ae9f6354f91ff792fd0d3636264b27a14d4/lib/llm/src/request_trace/agent_context.rs#L463-L475>) remains set until the old relay task observes cancellation, shuts down the relay, and reaches its final store at [lines 498–510](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/a5228ae9f6354f91ff792fd0d3636264b27a14d4/lib/llm/src/request_trace/agent_context.rs#L498-L510>).
* [`start_request_trace_tool_event_ingest`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/a5228ae9f6354f91ff792fd0d3636264b27a14d4/lib/llm/src/request_trace/agent_context.rs#L391-L460>) treats either guard collision as a successful start, so its caller receives no indication that the replacement generation owns neither task.

Depending on task scheduling, the replacement can lose the relay, the ingest subscriber, or both. Subsequent ZMQ tool events then fail to reach local request-trace sinks even though replacement initialization returned successfully.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable request tracing with tool records and a tool-event ZMQ endpoint.
2. Start runtime A and wait for both tool-event tasks to start.
3. Cancel runtime A, but hold its secondary tasks before their final guard-clearing stores.
4. Start runtime B and call `start_tool_event_ingest_from_policy` while both old guards remain set.
5. Allow runtime A's tasks to finish, then publish a tool event to the configured ZMQ endpoint.
6. Observe that runtime B has no relay or ingest task for the event, although its initialization returned `Ok(())`.

## Expected behavior

A replacement initialization should not treat a stopping generation as a reusable live generation. It should return only after the replacement owns functioning relay and ingest tasks, or after it has joined a generation that will remain live for the replacement.

## Suggested regression test

Use a controlled shutdown barrier to pause generation A immediately before each guard is released. Start generation B while A is paused, release A, and verify that a tool event traverses the replacement relay and ingest path. Exercise the relay and ingest guards separately because their cleanup can interleave.

This is distinct from #13372 and its linked PR ai-dynamo/dynamo#13382, which concern the sink-worker generation in `request_trace/sink.rs`; neither changes `request_trace/agent_context.rs` or these two task guards.

This report is based on source inspection of `upstream/main` at commit `a5228ae9f6354f91ff792fd0d3636264b27a14d4`. The controlled regression test has not yet been implemented or run in a deployed environment.

title: bug(multimodal): embedding-cache tasks prevent weak indexer eviction
body:
Implementation is under review in ai-dynamo/dynamo#14414, authored by git-jxj and still open on September 18, 2026. It addresses multimodal cache-indexer lifetime after consumer teardown. Statements in the original report about the absence of an applicable PR describe the earlier source-inspection state.

Review ownership reassigned to Rudy Pei (GitHub: PeaBrane) on September 18, 2026, at Matej’s request. Rudy is a router/runtime codeowner and contributed the endpoint-scoped transport and routing changes in the affected cache implementation. The next action is review and coordination of the existing contribution, consistent with [Keiven’s September 8 review/reassignment request](<https://nvidia.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0B1CRT1DT3/p1788912238437429>). The original defect description follows.

## Description

The multimodal embedding-cache indexer is registered through a `Weak` pointer, but two process-scoped background tasks retain strong `Arc` references to it. Dropping the last `PushRouter` therefore cannot release the indexer while the runtime remains active.

The ownership cycle is visible in the current implementation:

* [`SHARED_INDEXERS`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/kv_router/indexer/embedding_cache.rs#L56-L100>) stores `Weak<dyn MultimodalCacheIndex>` entries and prunes entries whose strong count reaches zero.
* [`start_subscriber`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/kv_router/indexer/embedding_cache.rs#L169-L253>) clones `Arc<Self>` into a task that reconnects until the runtime child token is cancelled. That task alone prevents the strong count from reaching zero.
* [`spawn_multimodal_cache_cleanup_watcher`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network/egress/push_router.rs#L419-L507>) also moves an `Arc<dyn MultimodalCacheIndex>` into a task. [`PushRouter::from_client_with_state`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network/egress/push_router.rs#L584-L643>) scopes that task to the runtime primary token rather than to the router that requested it.

After every router for a runtime endpoint is dropped, the indexer can therefore remain registered, retain its cache maps and discovery/event subscriptions, and be returned to a later router generation. The registry key is `(connection_id, endpoint_id)`, so a stable key retains one indexer rather than adding one per router; distinct retired keys can accumulate until runtime shutdown.

The instance-removal watcher lifecycle reports and fixes around `PushRouter` do not cover this object. In particular, PR ai-dynamo/dynamo#13224 explicitly left `spawn_multimodal_cache_cleanup_watcher` unchanged, and the current open PRs touching `push_router.rs` do not change this ownership path.

## Expected behavior

When no router consumes a runtime endpoint's multimodal cache index, the indexer and both associated watchers should stop and the weak registry entry should become prunable. A newly constructed router may then build a fresh indexer. Shared use by concurrent routers must continue to use one live indexer.

## Suggested regression test

Construct an indexer and cleanup watcher with a lifecycle that remains active, retain a `Weak<EmbeddingCacheIndexer>`, and drop the final external/router `Arc`. Assert that the weak pointer can no longer be upgraded and that both subscriptions stop. Repeat with a second router sharing the endpoint to verify that dropping only one consumer does not stop shared state.

This report is based on source inspection at commit `8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426`; it does not include a deployed reproduction.

title: bug(discovery): ModelManager retains endpoint runtime-config and HiCache state after teardown
body:
Implementation is under review in ai-dynamo/dynamo#14439, authored by git-jxj and still open on September 18, 2026. The revised implementation evicts idle runtime-config/HiCache state while retaining live consumers, including consumers that outlive their ModelManager, and includes lifecycle regressions.

Review ownership reassigned to Biswa Panda on September 18, 2026, at Matej’s request. Biswa is a runtime codeowner and owns the related discovery-watcher lifecycle issue [DGH-1360](<https://linear.app/nvidia/issue/DGH-1360>). The next action is review and coordination of the existing contribution, consistent with [Keiven’s September 8 review/reassignment request](<https://nvidia.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0B1CRT1DT3/p1788912238437429>). The original source report follows.

## Description

`ModelManager` keeps a runtime-config watch and, when HiCache is enabled, a `HicacheSharedKvCache` for every distinct `EndpointId`. Normal WorkerSet and discovery-group teardown removes models, cards, aliases, and topology state, but it does not remove either per-endpoint cache.

The retained state has active background work:

* [`runtime_configs` is explicitly manager-scoped](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager.rs#L171-L179>), and [`get_or_create_runtime_config_watcher`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager.rs#L2251-L2279>) stores each receiver until the manager is dropped. The [`runtime_config_watch` lifecycle contract](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/discovery/runtime_configs.rs#L105-L122>) explains how receiver and token lifetimes bound its discovery tasks.
* [`hicache_cache_for`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager.rs#L1793-L1813>) inserts a cache by endpoint and starts its Mooncake subscriber. The spawned task owns a cache clone and runs until cancellation or runtime-config closure ([subscriber implementation](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/kv_router/shared_cache.rs#L138-L147>), [run loop](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/kv_router/shared_cache.rs#L293-L369>)).
* [`remove_worker_set`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager.rs#L619-L637>) and [`remove_discovery_group`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager.rs#L878-L929>) do not release these entries. A manual [`remove_hicache_caches`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426/lib/llm/src/discovery/model_manager.rs#L1815-L1830>) method exists, but it has no production caller; there is no corresponding runtime-config removal path.

Consequently, a long-lived frontend that discovers and retires distinct endpoint IDs retains their watches, cache maps, and subscriber tasks until runtime shutdown. A stable endpoint ID reuses its entries, so this is endpoint-churn retention rather than per-request growth.

## Expected behavior

When the last model/discovery group using an endpoint is removed, the manager should eventually evict that endpoint's runtime-config and HiCache entries and cancel the associated tasks. The lifetime accounting must preserve sharing while multiple routers or WorkerSets still use the endpoint.

## Suggested regression test

Exercise creation and final teardown for a sequence of distinct endpoint IDs. After each final teardown, assert that the two manager maps no longer contain the endpoint and that the HiCache subscriber/runtime-config tasks have observed cancellation or released a weakly observed owner. The final map and task counts should remain bounded across the sequence.

This report is based on source inspection at commit `8097ac7b9ea636ff5983c4d9da16fd6bde84f426`; it does not include a deployed reproduction.

title: [FEATURE]: Document and test diffusion DGD deployments
body:
## Feature request

Update the diffusion documentation and examples so users can deploy every documented diffusion workflow through `DynamoGraphDeployment` (DGD), and make the local launch instructions transparent instead of presenting shell scripts as black boxes.

The operator and runtime are already expressive enough to represent the baseline workflows without a new DGD API or operator-controller change. The documentation should make that explicit and provide v1beta1 DGD examples for:

- Text-to-image
- Text-to-video
- Image-to-video
- Text-to-audio
- Text-to-text diffusion

At least one documented DGD path should exist for each workflow. Suggested baseline paths are:

| Workflow | Suggested DGD path |
|---|---|
| Text-to-image | SGLang FLUX, with vLLM-Omni as an additional example |
| Text-to-video | SGLang Wan or vLLM-Omni; cross-link the existing FastVideo DGD |
| Image-to-video | vLLM-Omni Wan I2V |
| Text-to-audio | vLLM-Omni Qwen3-TTS |
| Text-to-text diffusion | SGLang LLaDA |

### Show the commands behind local launch scripts

The workflow pages and local deployment examples currently show commands such as:

```bash
./launch/image_diffusion.sh
./launch/text-to-video-diffusion.sh
./launch/diffusion_llada.sh
bash examples/backends/vllm/launch/agg_omni_image.sh
```

These are useful convenience wrappers, but they hide the actual topology and backend flags. Each local example should show the expanded commands that the script launches, including:

- `python -m dynamo.frontend`
- The backend entrypoint (`dynamo.sglang`, `dynamo.vllm.omni`, `dynamo.trtllm`, or a custom worker)
- Model and modality flags
- Dynamo endpoint/discovery settings when relevant
- Media-storage configuration
- GPU or tensor-parallel requirements
- Any required environment variables

The script should remain available as the shortest launch path. The example should present it as an optional wrapper and link to the corresponding Recipes/CLI Templates/DGD page for the complete deployment shape.

### Add diffusion DGD documentation and recipes

Add a DGD section to the diffusion overview and each workflow page that covers:

1. A complete `nvidia.com/v1beta1` DGD manifest or a link to a checked-in recipe/template.
2. Frontend and worker component commands.
3. `backendFramework` selection and custom/no-op worker behavior.
4. Kubernetes discovery and the operator-injected Dynamo namespace.
5. Runtime image requirements and whether a stock release image or custom image is required.
6. Hugging Face credentials and model-cache PVC guidance.
7. GPU resources, shared memory, node selection, and multi-GPU requirements.
8. Media storage, public URL rewriting, retention, and cleanup.
9. A port-forward command and endpoint-specific smoke test.
10. A support matrix that distinguishes:
    - Expressible as DGD
    - Checked-in example available
    - Tested configuration
    - Experimental or custom-image requirement

Where practical, use a shared template for the aggregated vLLM-Omni workflows; image, video, I2V, and audio primarily differ by model, `--output-modalities`, resources, and request format.

### Clarify the support boundary

The docs should state that all five workflow types can be expressed as DGDs without operator code changes. They should separately identify the combinations that are not yet turnkey:

- TensorRT-LLM image/video diffusion requires a runtime containing the optional `visual_gen` module and may need a custom image.
- Disaggregated vLLM-Omni GLM-Image needs a multi-component DGD, stage configuration, NIXL connectors, GPU placement, and interconnect validation.
- SGLang image-to-video accepts `input_reference` in the handler, but the referenced launcher does not identify a tested I2V model or provide the promised I2V request example.
- Generated media needs an explicit object-storage or base64 strategy; pod-local `file://` URLs are not usable by remote clients.
- Diffusion-aware Planner/autoscaling behavior and scaling signals remain unvalidated.

### Suggested documentation and example scope

Likely affected areas include:

- `docs/fern/pages/use-cases/diffusion/overview.md`
- `docs/fern/pages/use-cases/diffusion/workflows/`
- SGLang and vLLM-Omni backend example/template pages
- `examples/backends/sglang/launch/`
- `examples/backends/vllm/launch/`
- `examples/diffusers/deploy/`
- New or existing Kubernetes recipe/template directories for diffusion

Acceptance criteria:

- Every workflow has at least one complete DGD path or an explicit explanation of the remaining blocker.
- Local docs display the underlying frontend and worker commands, not only a script invocation.
- Launch scripts remain available and are cross-linked with the relevant recipes/templates.
- Each DGD example includes a working endpoint smoke test.
- Media output guidance avoids presenting pod-local `file://` URLs as remotely retrievable URLs.
- The support matrix clearly separates DGD capability from test coverage and runtime-image availability.

## Describe the problem you're encountering

The current diffusion overview says that built-in diffusion backends use local CLI launch scripts and generally do not ship prebuilt Kubernetes recipes. This can be read as a missing operator capability, even though DGD is modality-agnostic and can run arbitrary frontend and worker commands with Kubernetes discovery.

A concrete v1beta1 SGLang FLUX DGD demonstrates the basic frontend-plus-worker shape. The repository also contains a v1beta1 FastVideo DGD with a custom worker. Source inspection shows that the built-in workers register the model types required by the frontend:

- vLLM-Omni registers image, video, and audio model types from `--output-modalities`.
- SGLang registers image and video generation workers and selects its text diffusion handler from `--dllm-algorithm`.
- The frontend exposes the corresponding image, video, audio, chat, and completion endpoints.

The gap is therefore primarily discoverability, command transparency, and checked-in DGD examples.

The local workflow documentation compounds the problem by showing only shell-script invocations. A user cannot tell from the page which processes are started, which flags are required, which settings belong to the frontend versus the worker, or how to translate the local launch into a DGD.

The existing examples also leave important operational behavior implicit:

- A worker using `--media-output-fs-url file:///...` returns a path local to that worker pod unless base64 output or object storage is configured.
- Generated media has no built-in TTL or garbage collection.
- A model-cache PVC mounted by both frontend and worker can cause a multi-attach failure when it is ReadWriteOnce and the pods land on different nodes; the frontend generally does not need that mount.
- SGLang diffusion compile configuration is not equivalent to passing the same-named LLM parser flag.
- Stock-image versus custom-image requirements are not summarized per backend.

Without DGD examples and expanded commands, users must reverse-engineer the shell scripts and backend source to discover that the operator already supports these deployment shapes.

## Describe alternatives you've tried

- Read every diffusion workflow page and followed the referenced launch scripts into the repository.
- Expanded the SGLang and vLLM-Omni launchers into their underlying frontend and worker commands.
- Inspected the v1beta1 DGD API and operator behavior for custom commands, backend detection, Kubernetes discovery, worker probes, PVCs, and repeated worker components.
- Compared a local SGLang FLUX DGD with the checked-in FastVideo DGD.
- Mapped each workflow to at least one existing backend that can register the required model type through a DGD.

This confirms that separate operator feature work is not required for the baseline aggregated paths. Maintaining private manifests or asking users to infer Kubernetes deployments from shell scripts would duplicate effort and continue to hide supported functionality, so checked-in recipes and documentation are preferable.

title: [BUG]: vllm-omni-audio-agg on 1.4.2 returns only the initial silent WAV chunk
body:
## Describe the bug

Case-level follow-up to #13383 and its [earlier validation report](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13383#issuecomment-5594559029). This issue tracks **`vllm-omni-audio-agg`** specifically so the corresponding local workflow and Kubernetes translation can have explicit pass/fail acceptance criteria.

On matched public Dynamo **1.4.2** images, startup/model discovery succeed, but `POST /v1/audio/speech` returns only the initial **0.08-second silent WAV chunk** even though the worker generates later non-silent audio.

**Release-specific scope:** #12100 already merged speech-streaming work. This is a 1.4.2 qualification/backport/support-boundary report, **not** a claim that current `main` still lacks that change.

## Local script and source DGD being mirrored

- **Originating local launcher:** [`examples/backends/vllm/launch/agg_omni_audio.sh`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/0873e6c52d13ebb571b7205b1eda7d523b2d5335/examples/backends/vllm/launch/agg_omni_audio.sh) (immutable upstream snapshot; byte-identical to the local script used as the template).
- **Candidate Kubernetes counterpart:** [`examples/backends/vllm/deploy/agg_omni_audio.yaml`](https://github.com/Jont828/dynamo/blob/72914d15522833cda4c449094c49698c95497ab9/examples/backends/vllm/deploy/agg_omni_audio.yaml) at example-branch commit `72914d15522833cda4c449094c49698c95497ab9`.
- The DGD counterpart is currently on the example branch, **not** a claim that this manifest ships in the 1.4.2 release or exists on upstream `main`.

The mapping preserves one frontend, one GPU worker, the model, output modality, media path, and relevant backend flags. The source script supplies local port/memory-budget helpers; Kubernetes supplies discovery/system-port wiring, placement, and an existing model-cache mount.

Core worker command represented in the DGD:

```bash
VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 \
python3 -m dynamo.vllm.omni \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice \
  --output-modalities audio \
  --media-output-fs-url file:///tmp/dynamo_media \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --enforce-eager
```

The frontend is the operator-managed equivalent of `python -m dynamo.frontend`.

## Deployment tested

The YAML below preserves the applied serving spec (images, commands, flags, GPU count, shared memory, media volume, and cache wiring). **Only infrastructure identifiers are redacted**: CPU/GPU pool values, existing PVC name, and cache subpath. Replace those placeholders with your environment's existing values; `hf-token-secret` is only a secret **reference**, never a token value. No cluster name, node identity, IP address, or credential is included.

<details>
<summary>Tested DGD, infrastructure identifiers redacted</summary>

```yaml
apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1beta1
kind: DynamoGraphDeployment
metadata:
  name: vllm-omni-audio-agg
spec:
  backendFramework: vllm
  components:
  - name: Frontend
    type: frontend
    replicas: 1
    podTemplate:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: main
          image: nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/dynamo-frontend:1.4.2
        nodeSelector:
          agentpool: replace-with-cpu-pool
  - name: OmniAudioWorker
    type: worker
    replicas: 1
    sharedMemorySize: 16Gi
    podTemplate:
      spec:
        containers:
        - name: main
          image: nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:1.4.2
          command:
          - python3
          - -m
          - dynamo.vllm.omni
          args:
          - --model
          - Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice
          - --output-modalities
          - audio
          - --media-output-fs-url
          - file:///tmp/dynamo_media
          - --trust-remote-code
          - --enforce-eager
          env:
          - name: VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN
            value: '1'
          - name: HF_HOME
            value: /model-cache
          envFrom:
          - secretRef:
              name: hf-token-secret
          resources:
            limits:
              nvidia.com/gpu: '1'
            requests:
              nvidia.com/gpu: '1'
          volumeMounts:
          - name: media-output
            mountPath: /tmp/dynamo_media
          - name: model-cache
            mountPath: /model-cache
            subPath: replace-with-cache-subpath
        volumes:
        - name: media-output
          emptyDir:
            sizeLimit: 20Gi
        - name: model-cache
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: replace-with-model-cache-pvc
        nodeSelector:
          agentpool: replace-with-gpu-pool
```
</details>

## Environment and version verification

Fresh reproduction on **September 10, 2026**, after release alignment:

- Dynamo operator/platform chart: **1.4.2**.
- Frontend: `nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/dynamo-frontend:1.4.2`.
- Worker: `nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:1.4.2`.
- Installed in both roles: `ai-dynamo==1.4.2`, `ai-dynamo-runtime==1.4.2`.
- Worker: `vllm==0.26.0`, `vllm-omni==0.26.0rc1`, `torch==2.11.0+cu130`.
- One NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3; driver `580.126.20`; Linux x86_64.
- CPU on the video codec probe: Intel Xeon Platinum 8480C.
- Actual running image identities were compared with fresh public registry manifests, not inferred from tag strings:
  - frontend tag/index digest: `sha256:80589311c904b82927ae95703c1bc59c49eb7ac10d25925c0e457260da915bc7`
  - worker tag/index digest: `sha256:b23ce9e87c413725024ddfd2e06c1e7da220eb48f8a93037f0b01d564b54bd13`

Server-side dry-run, both components' readiness, and `/v1/models` passed. This is a functional reproduction, not a performance benchmark. No source hot-patch or replacement runtime was used for the baseline request.
## Steps to reproduce

1. Save the DGD above as `deployment.yaml`, resolve the placement/cache placeholders, and use an existing namespace, model-cache PVC, and HF secret.
2. Deploy and wait for readiness:

   ```bash
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" apply --dry-run=server -f deployment.yaml
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" apply -f deployment.yaml
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" wait --for=condition=Ready dgd/vllm-omni-audio-agg --timeout=20m
   kubectl -n "$NAMESPACE" port-forward svc/vllm-omni-audio-agg-frontend 8000:8000
   ```

3. In another terminal, confirm `GET /v1/models` contains `Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice`, then send the request below. The exact saved request was replayed unchanged for the observed September 10 rerun.

Save as `request.json`:

```json
{
  "input": "Hey, this is generated using NVIDIA Dynamo.",
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice",
  "voice": "vivian",
  "language": "English",
  "data_source": "b64_json",
  "response_format": "wav"
}
```

```bash
curl --max-time 1200 -sS -D headers.txt \
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/audio/speech \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary @request.json -o output.wav
```

## Expected behavior

A complete WAV containing the requested utterance, or a correctly implemented streaming response preserving all audio chunks. The returned waveform must not consist solely of an initial silent chunk.

## Actual behavior

- HTTP **200**, `Content-Type: audio/wav`.
- Exactly **3,884 bytes**, mono 16-bit PCM, 24 kHz, 1,920 frames: **0.08 s**.
- RMS **0**, peak **0**, **0 nonzero samples**.
- SHA-256 `056e096196265b3e34608224a2e81e7c607daf5cadb366f5cd84d00c302b3350`, identical to the earlier failed run.
- For that same HTTP request, worker logs record three WAV chunks:

  ```text
  1920 samples, sr=24000, 3884 bytes wav
  48000 samples, sr=24000, 96044 bytes wav
  40320 samples, sr=24000, 80684 bytes wav
  ```

  That is 3.76 s of encoded worker output, but only the first 0.08 s reaches the HTTP caller.

A separate direct-to-worker request captured all three chunks: 0.08 s silent, 2.00 s non-silent, 0.72 s non-silent (2.80 s total). Its first chunk is byte-identical to the HTTP output. This proves subsequent worker audio exists; **it is not an end-to-end HTTP pass or a listening/transcription claim**.

**Important correction to the earlier umbrella report:** raw WAV is the intended frontend response here, even with `data_source=b64_json`. The absence of a JSON/base64 envelope is not the bug. Selecting only the first WAV is.

## Diagnosis and suggested scope

The [1.4.2 frontend speech handler](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/v1.4.2/lib/llm/src/http/service/openai.rs) folds the response stream, then selects `response.data.first()` and decodes only that item's base64 into the HTTP body. The [audio aggregator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/v1.4.2/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/audios/aggregator.rs) extends the data list; it does not concatenate complete waveform payloads into that first entry.

[PR #12100](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/12100), commit `a97afd2d51819f88d1033522312137b35feabc9d`, merged speech-streaming/compatibility work. It is present on the tested example branch but is **not an ancestor of tag v1.4.2**. Include the appropriate frontend and worker changes in matched images, then rerun this case. If backporting is not appropriate, explicitly document which image/release revision is required rather than marking the stock 1.4.2 DGD as working.

This is **not a missing CLI flag**: `--trust-remote-code`, `--enforce-eager`, and `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1` were already aligned with the launcher and present in the tested deployment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The versioned support boundary is explicit: validated fixed images or a clearly documented limitation/backport decision for 1.4.2.
- [ ] The same HTTP request returns the complete non-silent utterance, not just the initial 80 ms.
- [ ] Regression coverage exercises multiple audio chunks with a silent first chunk and verifies complete delivery/valid WAV framing.
- [ ] Frontend/worker compatibility is tested, rather than only replacing one side and assuming the protocol matches.
- [ ] Documentation uses `curl -o output.wav` for raw speech output and does not require a JSON envelope for this path.

## Validation boundary and cleanup

Only the stated stock-release failure and diagnostic comparisons have been verified. No patched end-to-end deployment is claimed. Temporary test DGDs were removed after capture; source/example code and shared controllers were not changed. Full local manifests, requests, redacted logs, runtime sources, media, hashes, and cleanup evidence were retained; private cluster diagnostics are intentionally not pasted into this public issue.

## Related case trackers

- #14667: `vllm-omni-video-agg`
- #14668: `vllm-omni-i2v-agg`
- #14669: `vllm-omni-audio-agg`

T2V and I2V share the field-propagation and codec root causes; these separate issues track each example's end-to-end qualification, not unrelated implementations of the same fix. Parent documentation/qualification tracker: #13383.

title: Streaming clients get HTTP 200 + a sanitized 500 frame for a request no worker can serve
body:
An implementation is available for review in ai-dynamo/dynamo#14788, authored by Prudctual; it remains open as of September 18, 2026 and explicitly closes GitHub issue [ai-dynamo/dynamo#14748](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/14748>). The proposal uses a 100 ms pre-stream error-peek window. Review that contract against the existing preference for validation before opening the stream; the proposed timing behavior is not yet an accepted resolution.

The merged ai-dynamo/dynamo#14467 addressed non-streaming error handling and does not close this streaming follow-up. The next action is review of the existing contribution.

## Problem

A streaming client that sends a request no worker can serve receives `HTTP 200` followed by an SSE frame reading `"Internal server error"`, with no indication of the real problem:

```
HTTP status: 200
data: {"error":{"message":"Internal server error","type":"internal_server_error","code":500}}
```

The same request with `"stream": false` correctly returns `400` with the worker's explanation. Streaming is the default in most OpenAI-compatible clients, so this is the common path.

## Cause

A capability guard raised inside a handler's async-generator body only executes on the first `__anext__`. By then `generate()` has returned a stream and the frontend has already committed `200`. `check_for_backend_error` is only consulted on the streaming path when `pre_commit_error_peek_timeout()` returns `Some`, and `DYN_HTTP_PRE_COMMIT_ERROR_PEEK_MS` is unset by default — `lib/llm/src/http/service/openai.rs` comments this as "Env var unset → skip peek, commit HTTP 200 immediately (pre-fix behavior)".

Setting `DYN_HTTP_PRE_COMMIT_ERROR_PEEK_MS=2000` yields `400` with the worker's reason for both streaming and non-streaming, confirming the mechanism works and is simply off.

## Options

1. **Default the peek window on** (e.g. 50–100ms) in `pre_commit_error_peek_timeout()`. One line, benefits every backend and every guard. Cost: a short delay before committing `200` on streaming requests — worth measuring.
2. **Refuse before the stream opens.** Hoist capability checks that need only the request and static config out of the generator body so they raise at call time. The refusal then travels in the typed response prologue (ai-dynamo/dynamo#14467) and the frontend sets the status before committing. For TRT-LLM the seam is `push_egress_capable`, which is already a plain `def` running at call time; SGLang has no equivalent seam today.

Option 2 makes the pre-stream typing added in ai-dynamo/dynamo#14467 pay off for Python backends, which it currently does not.

## Context

Follow-up to ai-dynamo/dynamo#14467, which fixed the non-streaming case.

title: Avoid publishing empty endpoint instance lists on local watcher cancellation
body:
The implementation is under review in [fix(runtime): preserve endpoint snapshot when watcher exits](https://linear.app/nvidia/review/fixruntime-preserve-endpoint-snapshot-when-watcher-exits-bc19cbf103a1), which explicitly closes GitHub issue [ai-dynamo/dynamo#12304](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/12304>). The PR remains open and was updated September 18, 2026 at head `82876b0b4fd4f73f7b926dc00b029c9aefe7366e`. Keep this ticket In Review; preserving a snapshot during local cancellation must continue to allow authoritative empty updates from discovery.

## Summary

Discovery endpoint watchers should not publish an empty instance list to local clients when the watcher is shutting down because the local runtime or HTTP frontend is cancelling.

## Motivation

During graceful frontend shutdown, in-flight request handlers may still need the last known endpoint instances while the HTTP server drains. If a local discovery watcher publishes an empty list as part of its own cancellation path, those in-flight requests can incorrectly treat a healthy router/backend as unavailable and fail with errors like "instance not found and no other instances available".

This is a generic shutdown/discovery invariant: local watcher teardown should not look like an authoritative remote deletion unless discovery actually observed the endpoint becoming empty.

## Expected behavior

* On local cancellation/shutdown of the endpoint watcher, preserve the last known snapshot or otherwise distinguish local watcher termination from an authoritative empty discovery update.
* Continue publishing real empty snapshots when discovery genuinely reports that all instances are gone.
* In-flight request drains should be able to complete using existing endpoint state until the graceful drain ends or the request itself is cancelled.
* Logs/metrics should make local watcher cancellation distinguishable from remote endpoint removal.

## Reproduction scenario

1. Start a synthetic frontend and one synthetic backend/router instance.
2. Begin a long-running dummy streaming request, for example with prompt text "synthetic long request" and no customer data.
3. Trigger graceful shutdown of the frontend while allowing HTTP drain to continue.
4. The local endpoint watcher should stop without publishing an authoritative empty instance list to the in-flight handler.
5. The in-flight request should not fail solely because the local watcher cancelled.

Please keep reproductions fully synthetic: fake endpoint names, fake request IDs, no real prompts, no customer identifiers, no internal URLs, and no credentials.

title: [BUG]: tool_call_dispatch cannot safely reconstruct fragmented arguments
body:
The implementation is under review in [fix(frontend): stop tool_call_dispatch handing harnesses truncated arguments](https://linear.app/nvidia/review/fixfrontend-stop-tool-call-dispatch-handing-harnesses-truncated-ea892c1d3c5d), which explicitly closes GitHub issue [ai-dynamo/dynamo#13972](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/13972>). The PR remains open and its current head is `4aa5dc191982e925bcc262c4e06ffdd2cfc3a4f3`, updated September 17 and checked September 18, 2026. Keep this ticket In Review until the change is delivered; the original protocol requirements below remain the review scope.

## Summary

The opt-in Chat Completions `tool_call_dispatch` extension cannot safely consume fragmented OpenAI tool-call deltas. It currently treats one chunk containing `id`, `function.name`, and `Some(function.arguments)` as a complete call, emits that chunk as `event: tool_call_dispatch`, and immediately deduplicates the call by `(choice_index, id)`.

That same-chunk assumption is contradicted by Dynamo's own stream aggregation code and becomes operationally important when #13821 restores immediate publication of Python vLLM tool-call fragments.

The Rust dispatcher must accumulate each call by outer choice index and inner tool-call index, preserve identity fields across chunks, append argument fragments, and emit exactly once only at a defined JSON completion boundary.

## Current behavior and failure modes

The current predicate is in [`streaming_tool_dispatch_events`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ff18f7210d9909d824b41193e1a58bb77e87d1c8/lib/llm/src/http/service/openai.rs#L2635-L2681>):

```rust
let has_name_and_args = chunk
    .function
    .as_ref()
    .is_some_and(|f| f.name.is_some() && f.arguments.is_some());

if let (true, Some(id)) = (has_name_and_args, &chunk.id) {
    if !dispatched_ids.insert((choice.index, id.clone())) {
        continue;
    }
    // emit the current chunk
}
```

OpenAI tool-call chunks require the inner `index`, but `id`, `type`, `function`, `function.name`, and `function.arguments` may arrive independently. Dynamo already documents and handles the common shape elsewhere:

```text
delta 1: index + id + type + function.name
delta 2: index + first function.arguments fragment
delta N: index + final function.arguments fragment
```

The current dispatcher therefore has three distinct failures:

1. If the identity opener contains `arguments: Some("")`, the existing intentional empty-argument rule dispatches an empty call immediately. Later fragments cannot correct it because the ID is already in the dedup set.
2. If the opener contains ID/name with `arguments: None` and continuation chunks contain arguments without repeating ID/name, no event is ever emitted because no individual chunk contains all three fields.
3. If one chunk contains ID/name and a non-empty but incomplete prefix such as `{"path":"/a/very`, that invalid prefix is dispatched immediately and later completion is suppressed.

This is not only hypothetical backend behavior. [`DeltaAggregator::merge_tool_call_chunk`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ff18f7210d9909d824b41193e1a58bb77e87d1c8/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs#L209-L254>), added by ai-dynamo/dynamo#8582 for #8640, already corrects the same same-chunk assumption for non-streaming aggregation: ID/type/name are first-wins and argument fragments concatenate by inner tool-call index. Its split and interleaved regression cases are at [lines 1259-1423](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ff18f7210d9909d824b41193e1a58bb77e87d1c8/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs#L1259-L1423>).

## Required behavior

The ordinary OpenAI `data:` chunks must pass through unchanged. With `--enable-streaming-tool-dispatch`, Dynamo must additionally emit one `tool_call_dispatch` event containing the fully assembled call as soon as the completion policy below is satisfied.

The event remains a Dynamo extension with its current payload:

```json
{
  "choice_index": 0,
  "tool_call": {
    "index": 0,
    "id": "call_1",
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
      "name": "create_file",
      "arguments": "{\"path\":\"/a/very/long/file\"}"
    }
  }
}
```

It must not be converted into a synthetic ordinary `ChatCompletionChunk`, and it must not be enabled by default on `/v1/chat/completions`.

### 1. Request-local assembly state

Replace the HashSet-only detector with request-local state keyed by:

```rust
(choice.index, tool_call_chunk.index)
```

This state belongs beside the current reasoning and dispatch state in the per-request streaming branch at [`openai.rs:2935-2941`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ff18f7210d9909d824b41193e1a58bb77e87d1c8/lib/llm/src/http/service/openai.rs#L2935-L2941>). Create or update an entry for every tool-call chunk; do not require ID and name to coexist in the chunk that creates the entry.

For normal fragments, use the same merge semantics as `DeltaAggregator`:

* Preserve the first non-`None` ID, type, and function name.
* Append every `Some(arguments)` fragment in arrival order, including empty fragments.
* Allow arguments to arrive before identity and dispatch later when both identity and completion are available.
* If a later non-empty identity field conflicts with an earlier value for the same key, mark the entry invalid, log the producer violation, and do not assemble a call from conflicting identities.

Retain a completed-key tombstone after emission so a replayed complete chunk cannot emit twice. Isolation must remain correct when two choices use the same call ID and the same inner index.

The existing merge helper should be extracted for shared use, or the dispatcher should have parity tests against it. Do not introduce a third, subtly different field-merge policy.

### 2. Early-completion policy

Chat Completions has no per-tool-call `done` bit. `finish_reason` terminates the choice, not each individual call. Consequently, JSON closure is a Dynamo early-dispatch convention rather than proof supplied by the OpenAI protocol.

For early dispatch before `finish_reason`:

* Maintain an incremental JSON structural scanner with container, string, and escape state that survives fragment boundaries.
* At minimum, recognize self-delimiting top-level objects and arrays, including nested mixed containers.
* Ignore braces/brackets inside strings and handle an escape split across chunks.
* Consume the entire current fragment before declaring a candidate, so `{}junk` cannot dispatch at the first closing brace.
* When the root container closes, validate the complete accumulated string once with `serde_json`, allowing only trailing whitespace.
* Emit only when JSON syntax is valid and ID/name are available.

The scanner should be O(total argument bytes). Calling `serde_json::from_str` on the whole buffer after every token would become quadratic for the long arguments that motivated #13821. Structural scanning identifies candidate boundaries; `serde_json` confirms them.

Top-level scalar values do not need speculative early dispatch. They can wait for the terminal policy below, because a number such as `1` may legally receive another fragment such as `2`.

Successful JSON parsing proves syntax only. It does not validate arguments against the requested tool schema or authorize execution; extension clients must continue to perform those checks.

Once a valid root value has been dispatched, a later non-whitespace continuation for that key is a backend/protocol violation. Log and suppress it; an already emitted event cannot be retracted. Preserve the existing behavior for an exact replay of an already completed call without emitting a duplicate.

### 3. Terminal, empty, and malformed state

`Some("")` is ambiguous during streaming: it may mean a parameterless backend call, or it may be an empty opener followed by real argument fragments. It must not dispatch early merely because the field is present.

* Canonical parameterless arguments (`"{}"`) can dispatch early.
* On `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, make one final completion pass. This is the only point where the existing empty-string parameterless compatibility may be preserved safely, because the choice has definitively stopped producing arguments.
* Preserve the exact accumulated argument string in the event; do not silently rewrite model output.
* Do not dispatch incomplete or malformed non-empty JSON on `length`, backend error, disconnect, or raw EOF.
* Clear unfinished state for each choice when that choice terminates. Request-local state naturally disappears when the HTTP stream is dropped.

### 4. Pipeline placement and ordering

Keep dispatch at its current observational boundary in the HTTP stream:

1. Apply `parallel_tool_calls=false` filtering.
2. Update dispatch state from the surviving ordinary chunk.
3. Emit `tool_call_dispatch` before the ordinary `data:` event for the fragment that completes the call, matching current ordering.
4. Pass the original response once through `EventConverter`, metrics, and response collection.

The relevant loop is [`openai.rs:2947-3024`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ff18f7210d9909d824b41193e1a58bb77e87d1c8/lib/llm/src/http/service/openai.rs#L2947-L3024>). The tracker may clone or accumulate metadata for its own payload, but it must not consume, rewrite, duplicate, or re-aggregate the standard deltas.

## Prior art from [#6845](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/6845>)

[#6845](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/6845>) is useful design material, not a patch to cherry-pick. Its final implementation provided:

* Request-local `(choice_index, tool_call_index)` state.
* Accumulated arguments.
* String and escape state across fragment boundaries.
* Exactly-once emission.
* Tests for quoted braces, split escapes, multi-fragment ordering, and interleaved calls.

Do not restore its old stream adapter or `event: tool_call.complete`; the current `tool_call_dispatch` event boundary is the correct integration point. Do not copy its scanner unchanged either: it initialized state only when ID and name appeared together, recognized only object braces, did not parse the resulting JSON, and considered `}{"x":1}` structurally complete after clamping the leading brace. The new regressions should reject that input.

## Regression coverage

Add focused tests that establish both the state machine and its placement in the SSE pipeline:

 1. A valid single-chunk object still emits exactly once with the existing payload.
 2. An identity opener followed by two argument-only fragments emits nothing until the final fragment, then contains the preserved index/ID/type/name and complete arguments.
 3. `arguments: Some("")` followed by later fragments does not dispatch the empty opener.
 4. ID, name, and arguments arriving in different chunks still assemble correctly; conflicting repeated identity fails closed.
 5. Quoted braces, escaped quotes, a backslash split across fragments, nested objects, and arrays do not create false boundaries.
 6. Leading junk, trailing junk in the completing fragment, mismatched containers, and truncated JSON never dispatch.
 7. Two same-choice calls at inner indexes 0 and 1 can interleave and complete in reverse order.
 8. Two outer choices can both use inner index 0 and the same call ID without state collision.
 9. `parallel_tool_calls=false` never accumulates or emits a filtered higher-index call.
10. Terminal cases cover valid JSON, `{}`, absent/empty arguments under the compatibility rule, invalid JSON, and `finish_reason: "length"`.
11. A repeated complete backend chunk remains deduplicated.
12. A stream-level test proves that every #13821-style ordinary fragment remains an ordinary SSE `data:` event and that exactly one dispatch event precedes the ordinary fragment that completes the JSON.

The existing `make_choice_with_tool_call` helper hardcodes inner index 0 and should accept an explicit tool-call index. The current `extract_sse_data_json` test helper also finds JSON boundaries with a brace-only, string-unaware scan; quoted-brace cases should exercise typed state/payloads or the actual SSE serialization rather than failing inside that test helper.

## Documentation

Update the streaming-dispatch documentation to state the actual completion convention: Dynamo assembles fragments and JSON-syntax validates the complete argument string before emitting the extension event, while the client remains responsible for tool-schema validation and execution policy. The existing claim that the harness receives a ready-to-execute call with no assembly should remain true after this change.

## Scope

This issue covers only the Rust Chat Completions `tool_call_dispatch` extension.

* #13821 separately restores normal OpenAI delta cadence in the Python vLLM postprocessor.
* Parser-v2 Qwen streaming is separate because its scanner currently waits for a complete `</function>` block.
* Responses and Anthropic converters use their own protocol completion events and are not changed here.
* The custom Chat Completions event remains opt-in; this issue does not make it part of the standard OpenAI stream.

cc @keivenchang @rmccorm4

title: bug(c-api): init after shutdown reuses canceled runtime and stale publisher
body:
ai-dynamo/dynamo#13379 is open for review as of September 18, 2026. Its implementation defines process-once C API initialization, rejects incompatible or post-shutdown initialization, and addresses shutdown during discovery and publication after shutdown. This is the explicit-rejection alternative in the original report, rather than support for restarting the process-global runtime.

The remaining work is review and completion of that PR. The original source inspection and proposed behavior below are retained as the defect record; they should not be read as evidence that no implementation now exists.

## Description

The C API's `dynamo_llm_shutdown` cancels the initialized runtime but leaves every initialization singleton populated. A subsequent `dynamo_llm_init` therefore reuses the canceled `Worker`/`DistributedRuntime` and the first call's `KvEventPublisher` instead of constructing usable state or returning a deterministic error.

The relevant state is process-global:

* [`WK`, `DRT`, and `KV_PUB`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675/lib/bindings/c/src/lib.rs#L32-L41>) are non-resettable `OnceCell`s.
* [`dynamo_llm_init`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675/lib/bindings/c/src/lib.rs#L115-L197>) uses `get_or_try_init` for all three. Once populated, later namespace, component, endpoint, and block-size arguments do not replace the stored publisher.
* [`dynamo_llm_shutdown`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675/lib/bindings/c/src/lib.rs#L199-L211>) calls `wk.runtime().shutdown()` and returns `OK`; it does not clear or mark the cells unusable.
* [`Runtime::shutdown`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675/lib/runtime/src/runtime.rs#L324-L365>) asynchronously cancels the runtime's endpoint and primary tokens. Cancellation is irreversible for that runtime instance.

On an `init(A) -> shutdown() -> init(B)` sequence, the second call can wait indefinitely for discovery through the retired `DRT`, or it can return `OK` while retaining canceled runtime state and publisher A. It cannot produce a fresh publisher for B. Even if reinitialization is intentionally unsupported, returning `OK` or hanging is misleading; the API should reject the second initialization explicitly.

## Expected behavior

The API should either support a complete `init -> shutdown -> init` lifecycle by replacing all runtime- and endpoint-scoped state, or define initialization as process-once and return `ERR` immediately after shutdown or for incompatible repeated arguments. It should not report success with canceled or stale state.

## Suggested regression test

Exercise the exported API through a testable state holder or a subprocess fixture: initialize endpoint A, shut it down and await the shutdown boundary, then initialize endpoint B. If restart is supported, assert that B has a non-cancelled runtime and a publisher configured for B. If the API is intentionally one-shot, assert that the second call returns `ERR` promptly. Also cover a repeated live initialization with different endpoint arguments so those arguments cannot be silently ignored.

This report is based on source inspection at commit `f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675`; the regression test has not yet been implemented or run against a deployed C consumer.

title: PushRouter: shared endpoint watcher leaves the backend list_and_watch task running past its own cancellation
body:
Cancelled as an obsolete branch-specific defect on September 18, 2026. ai-dynamo/dynamo#13224 was closed without merging on September 8. Matej’s closing explanation states that the cancellation leak reported here was introduced by that branch, and that no independently justified subset of the rewrite had a demonstrated current-main requirement.

The report below remains historical evidence about the abandoned branch. A future correction should start from a reproduced defect on then-current main, rather than treating the closed rewrite as pending delivery.

Follow-up from review on [https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13224](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13224>) (line 610 of `lib/runtime/src/pipeline/network/egress/push_router.rs`).

`spawn_endpoint_watcher_task` exits its fan-out loop on `lifecycle.cancelled()`, so the shared `EndpointWatcher` stops handing out `on_instance_added`/`on_instance_removed` once the last subscribed router drops. But the call that starts the underlying stream, `endpoint.drt().discovery().list_and_watch(query.clone(), None)`, passes `None` for its own cancellation token, so the backend watch (the KV-store or Kubernetes watch task under it) is tied only to the discovery client's own default token, not to `lifecycle`. Dropping the last router for an endpoint stops the fan-out loop but leaves that backend watch task running until a later event on the same query or until runtime shutdown.

Fix: build a per-subscription `CancellationToken` that is cancelled when either `cancel_token` or `lifecycle` cancels, and pass `Some(that_token)` to `list_and_watch` instead of `None`.

cc @PeaBrane @GuanLuo

title: bug(request-trace): sink workers cannot restart after runtime shutdown
body:
Resolved by ai-dynamo/dynamo#14642, merged September 14, 2026. The merged sink lifecycle serializes replacement, drains cancelled workers, and reopens the worker-start gate; its lifecycle regression covers reopening that gate. This resolves the original restart defect described below.

The original ai-dynamo/dynamo#13382 remains open, but its current diff contains only `benchmarks/router/common.py`. Its request-trace title and closing reference need separate reconciliation; that unrelated residual change does not keep this defect open. Delivery and request states were checked September 18, 2026.

## Description

Request-trace sink workers cannot be started again after their first runtime-scoped shutdown. The process-global `WORKERS_STARTED` guard is set before the workers are spawned, but it is cleared only when initial construction fails—not when the spawned workers finish.

The lifecycle is visible in the current implementation:

* [`WORKERS_STARTED`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675/lib/llm/src/request_trace/sink.rs#L20-L34>) is a process-global `AtomicBool`.
* [`spawn_workers_from_env`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675/lib/llm/src/request_trace/sink.rs#L226-L239>) changes it from `false` to `true` and resets it only if `spawn_workers` returns an error.
* Each [sink worker exits when its supplied cancellation token fires](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675/lib/llm/src/request_trace/sink.rs#L241-L290>), drains the receiver, and shuts down the sink. None of those exit paths clears the guard, and their `JoinHandle`s are discarded.
* A later [`init_from_env_with_shutdown`](<https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675/lib/llm/src/request_trace/mod.rs#L54-L83>) call treats the guard-induced no-op as success, marks capture active, and logs that request tracing initialized.

Consequently, after an in-process distributed-runtime/input generation is shut down, a replacement generation receives no request-trace sink workers. Trace publication can appear enabled while the broadcast bus has no sink receivers, silently losing subsequent records.

The guard is still needed to prevent concurrent input initializations from duplicating sink workers. Its ownership must therefore represent a complete worker generation and release only after every worker in that generation has stopped.

## Expected behavior

After the first generation's cancellation and sink shutdown complete, a later initialization should start one new set of sink workers. Overlapping initialization calls during a live generation should continue to share that generation rather than spawn duplicates.

## Suggested regression test

Start a worker generation with a recording sink and cancellation token, publish one record, then cancel the token and wait for the sink's shutdown notification. Start a second generation with a fresh token, publish another record, and assert that the second sink receives it. A concurrent-start assertion should verify that two live initializers still produce only one generation.

This report is based on source inspection at commit `f6f99696d2b0f83820ee81ae0588e208f117f675`; the regression test has not yet been implemented or run in a deployed environment.

title: Preserve externally managed LPX replica count across PodCliqueSet replacement
body:
## Summary

When an LPX component omits `replicas`, a `PodCliqueSet` replacement can lose the externally managed `PodCliqueScalingGroup` replica count. The replacement can then default to one replica.

## Required changes

Update the LPX workload-shape replacement flow to retain the observed native scaling-group replica count before the current `PodCliqueSet` is deleted. Carry that count into the replacement materialization and LPUPipelineRequest generation path.

Explicit component `replicas` must remain authoritative.

## Rationale

The current behavior can reduce engine capacity after a workload-shape change. It can also leave the workload unavailable.

## Affected areas

- `deploy/operator/internal/controller/lpx/lifecycle.go`
- LPX materialization and replacement tests under `deploy/operator/internal/controller/lpx/`

## Acceptance criteria

- If an LPX component omits `replicas`, a replacement `PodCliqueSet` uses the previously observed externally managed `PodCliqueScalingGroup` replica count.
- The replacement creates the corresponding number of LPUPipelineRequests.
- Explicit component `replicas` override the externally managed count.
- Tests cover replacement after an omitted-replicas deployment has a non-default scaling-group replica count.

## Backlinks

- Pull request: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/15062
- Review comment: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/15062#discussion_r4049895535
- Requested by: @andrewpaprotsky

title: fix(llm): request-payload audit record loses response and misreports payload_complete on mid-stream/admission error
body:
## Summary

When a streaming chat-completion request ends in an error — a mid-stream backend failure, a guided-decoding/grammar rejection, a client cancel, or an immediate admission-time rejection (e.g. a worker-capacity 503) — the request-payload audit record written for compliance/logging purposes omits the `response` field entirely, **but still reports `payload_complete: true` and `payload_drop_reason: null`**, as if nothing were missing.

## Why this is a problem

`RequestPayloadHandle::emit()` hardcodes both fields regardless of whether a response was actually produced:

https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/request_trace/payload.rs#L76-L94

```rust
/// Publish one request trace payload record. Consumes the handle to enforce
/// exactly one payload record per request. `response` is `None` on client
/// cancel / gateway timeout / aggregation failure; the record still carries
/// the request so those cases remain inspectable.
pub fn emit(self, response: Option<Arc<NvCreateChatCompletionResponse>>) {
    super::record::emit_request_payload(
        super::RequestTracePayload {
            request_id: self.request_id,
            endpoint: "openai.chat_completion".to_string(),
            model: self.model,
            request: Some(self.request),
            response,
            http_request_headers: self.http_request_headers,
            payload_complete: true,
            payload_drop_reason: None,
        },
        unix_time_ms(self.event_time),
    );
}
```

The doc comment already acknowledges `response` can legitimately be `None` — but `payload_complete`/`payload_drop_reason` were never wired to reflect that.

`response` gets `None` whenever `DeltaAggregator::apply` fails to aggregate the collected stream chunks:

https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/request_trace/payload_stream.rs#L59-L114

`DeltaAggregator::apply` uses `try_fold` over `Annotated::into_data()`, which returns `Err` for any chunk flagged as an error event:

https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs#L331-L337

https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/runtime/src/protocols/annotated.rs#L99-L104

`try_fold` short-circuits on the first `Err`, discarding all previously-accumulated content — proven intentional-but-narrow by the aggregator's own test:

https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs#L2609-L2644 (`preserves_typed_error_after_partial_output` — feeds a partial-content chunk followed by an error chunk and asserts the whole call returns `Err`, losing the partial text)

`RequestPayloadHandle` is created from the pristine inbound request the moment it arrives at the frontend, before dispatch to any worker — so this isn't limited to mid-generation failures; an immediate admission-time rejection (e.g. a worker returning 503 before any token is generated) goes through the identical path and produces the identical misleadingly-"complete" record.

`response` and `payload_drop_reason` are both `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, while `payload_complete` is not optional:

https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/request_trace/types.rs#L57-L72

So the emitted JSONL/NATS/OTEL record for a failed request simply omits the `response` key while asserting `"payload_complete": true` — indistinguishable from a genuinely complete record to any downstream consumer that checks the flag rather than key presence. This directly undermines the audit/compliance use case the payload-capture feature exists for: a request whose response the client actually received over SSE can end up with **no recorded response at all**, silently, with no truncation or drop-reason marker.

This was found while investigating NVBugs 6705092 (sporadic multi-hour gaps in Kratos-ingested request/response payload logs for a production NVCF-hosted Dynamo deployment). No customer/deployment detail from that investigation is included here.

## Proposed fix

- Set `payload_complete: false` and populate `payload_drop_reason` (e.g. `"aggregation_failed"`, `"client_cancelled"`, or the underlying error message) in `RequestPayloadHandle::emit` whenever `response` is `None`, instead of hardcoding `true`/`None`.
- Consider giving `DeltaAggregator::apply` (or a payload-capture-specific variant) a mode that returns whatever partial content was accumulated before the error, alongside the error, rather than discarding it via `try_fold`'s short-circuit — so a request that streamed real content before failing doesn't lose that content from the audit trail.
- Add a test in `payload_stream.rs`/`request_trace/` that feeds a partial-content chunk followed by an error chunk (mirroring `preserves_typed_error_after_partial_output`) and asserts the emitted `RequestTracePayload` has `payload_complete: false` with a populated `payload_drop_reason` — there's currently no coverage of this path in that module.
- Separately worth checking: audit-payload capture appears wired only for the chat-completions endpoint (`create_handle`/`emit` call sites); the legacy `/v1/completions` path may have no equivalent capture at all, which would be a related but distinct gap.

## Links
- https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/request_trace/payload.rs#L76-L94
- https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/request_trace/payload_stream.rs#L21-L116
- https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs#L331-L337
- https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/protocols/openai/chat_completions/aggregator.rs#L2609-L2644
- https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/runtime/src/protocols/annotated.rs#L99-L104
- https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/ce48476ff9b95a6de7dbe64c952e1b2049e1cc72/lib/llm/src/request_trace/types.rs#L57-L72
